llm.summary: The skill's requirements, instructions, and templates are internally consistent with a relationship-outreach drafting assistant and it does not request extra credentials or installs.

dimensions.detail: The name and description (detect signals, rank them, draft messages) match the SKILL.md and the included templates. It expects signals from calendar, email, messaging, browser tabs and user-provided context — which is coherent for a relationship assistant. The skill does not ask for unrelated credentials or binaries.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md limits data use to contexts the user provides or explicitly makes available, repeatedly states drafts require user approval, and instructs not to invent evidence. It does not direct the agent to read arbitrary filesystem paths, hidden tokens, or to transmit data to external endpoints beyond ordinary drafting. (It does assume access to user-provided calendars/email/messages/browser tabs — the skill relies on the host/agent connectors for that, not its own declared secrets.)
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: Instruction-only skill with no install spec and no code files — nothing is downloaded or written to disk by the skill itself. This is low-risk from an install perspective.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables, credentials, or config paths. That is proportionate to the described behavior; any access to calendars, email, or messaging is expected to come via the platform's connectors or explicit user-provided data rather than skill-level secrets.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always is false, the skill is user-invocable and not force-included. There is no instruction to modify other skills or system-wide settings. It does not request permanent presence or elevated privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance:
This skill appears coherent and low-risk as an instruction-only drafting assistant, but check these before installing:
- Confirm how the host/agent will provide calendar, email, and messaging data: will the agent use platform connectors automatically or only when you explicitly share content? Require explicit consent for each source if you want control.
- Verify the 'never sends anything' promise in practice: test that drafts are never transmitted without your explicit approval and check what UI action actually triggers sending.
- Review the linked GitHub repo (homepage) for any additional code or instructions not included in the skill bundle and watch for any later changes that add install scripts or network endpoints.
- Decide what personal data you are comfortable sharing (contact lists, message history, calendar events) and test with dummy or non-sensitive data first.
- If you care about retention or logging, ask the platform/developer whether any drafts or parsed signals are stored server-side and for how long.
If you want lower-risk usage, only provide individual messages, browser tabs, or exported contact lines as needed rather than granting blanket access to inboxes or calendars.
